confirmed.statement: S1 explicitly reports 60 participants randomly assigned in a between-subjects experiment, with participants organized into teams of three.

The paper reports 30 people recruited per arm, ten teams of three per arm, and 60 people taking part; Tables 3-4 contain 30 distinct participant IDs per arm (C1-C30 and G1-G30). These are people, not teams, sessions, or ratings.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 16, Section 4.4; p. 42, Appendix C; pp. 43-44, Tables 3-4.

confirmed.statement: The questionnaire analysis explicitly reports N=60 and n=30 per arm. This supports participants.n_analyzed=60 and both arms.n_analyzed=30 as reported questionnaire counts, which is the scope expressly stated in the form.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 17, Section 4.5.1; p. 20, Section 5.2; pp. 41-42, Appendix A, Tables 1-2 and notes.

confirmed.statement: Arm-specific randomization-stage counts are not separately labeled: 30 per arm is reported for recruitment, participation, and questionnaire analysis. The form conservatively leaves both arms.n_randomized null.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Section 4.1 and Figure 5; p. 16, Section 4.4; p. 42, Appendix C.

confirmed.statement: No participant exclusion rule, attrition count, or explanation for the smaller story set is reported. Figure 5 shows task, survey, and interview stages without participant-flow counts; the form does not equate unreported attrition with zero attrition.
confirmed.locator: Whole-document review, especially PDF pp. 13-17, Sections 4.1-4.5 and Figure 5; pp. 41-44, Appendices A-C; pp. 50-51, Appendices G-H.

confirmed.statement: Content analysis uses nine FIERO texts and nine control texts despite ten recruited teams per arm. The paper does not identify the omitted texts/teams or state the people represented by the analyzed texts, so the form correctly leaves that headcount unknown.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 16, Sections 4.3-4.4; p. 17, Section 4.5.2; pp. 43-44, Tables 3-4.

confirmed.statement: The denominator 81 belongs to pairwise story comparisons, not people: each of nine texts in one arm is compared with each of nine in the other, using AB/BA evaluations. The form does not count these comparisons or the three LLM judges as participants.

Only one human randomized study is reported. Its practice session, three writing rounds, questionnaires, and interviews concern the same study cohort; Appendix G supplies no additional human sample to add to the count.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 13-17, Sections 4.1-4.5; pp. 50-51, Appendix G.

confirmed.statement: No reuse of another paper's participants or cross-paper shared sample is disclosed. The empty sample-overlap field is not evidence that overlap is impossible.
confirmed.locator: Whole-document review, PDF pp. 1-51, especially pp. 13-17, Sections 4.1-4.5; pp. 42-44, Appendix C; p. 51, Appendix H.

confirmed.statement: Source-level arithmetic caveat: Table 2 labels n=30 per arm, but its first-item means, 6.15 and 6.19, cannot be rounded means of 30 unweighted integer responses on the stated seven-point scale. The nearest possibilities are 6.13/6.17 and 6.17/6.20, respectively; missingness or response processing is not explained. This does not establish a replacement study-level headcount or show that the form mistranscribed the explicitly reported N.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 14, Section 4.2.1 (response scale); p. 41, Table 2, first CSI item. Arithmetic check: adjacent integer totals divided by 30 are 184/30 and 185/30 for GAME, and 185/30 and 186/30 for CONTROL.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds on the explicitly reported study-level questionnaire analysis of 60 people in this one randomized experiment. This verdict does not assign 60 people to the scored-story estimates.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Section 4.1; p. 17, Sections 4.5.1-4.5.2; p. 41, Table 1; creativity-codebook.md, Sections 3 and 7.

summary: The PDF explicitly reports 60 randomized people and questionnaire analyses of 30 per arm, supporting criterion 2 and the form's counts as reported. The scored-story headcount remains unknown, and inconsistent questionnaire item means prevent independent reconstruction of the analyzed sample.
